body.objective: Determine whether the quartic-completion ambiguity of the repaired Berger common action is removable presentation freedom or produces inequivalent q3 operations and relational detector responses.
body.stop_condition: When pulled, import the terminal certificate and exact action family from observer-post-common-action-frontier-input-pinned by content hash, regardless of whether that item constructs a complete quartic family or lands its first bounded obstruction. If a complete family exists, parameterize its real Berger-invariant quartic-completion space modulo total derivatives, field redefinitions, cyclic canonical transformations and terms vanishing to fourth order on the declared background. Derive q3 from every orbit representative, compute the complete arity-three identity, odd cyclicity and K_Berger-equivariance defects as polynomial functions on the completion moduli, and classify the exact admissible subvariety. Then propagate each surviving class into the same-action apparatus, memory and two-event emitter/receiver detector maps and determine which response tensors, ranks and frequency-shift observables are invariant across completion orbits. Land either a unique admissible orbit with one fully replayed nonlinear relational observable, a nontrivial moduli theorem with completion-independent observables, or an exact witness that the observable prediction depends on undetermined quartic data. If the imported item instead stops at a bounded module obstruction, prove whether adjoining the smallest named missing representation can change that obstruction before enlarging derivative order. Supply exact certificates, independent verifier, orbit-changing and observable-changing mutations, and an observer-atlas lifecycle update.
body.current_gate: quartic-completion moduli, q3 equivalence and completion-independent nonlinear observables
body.forbid: no arbitrary choice of quartic completion called canonical; no q3 imported from an action outside the classified family; no quotient by field redefinitions without transporting the pairing and detector map; no coordinate-frequency ratio called redshift; no prescribed external clock called a dynamical observer; no raw-D claim where only K_Berger acts; no completion-dependent response presented as a theory prediction; no particle, positivity, quantum, scattering, phenomenology or all-orders promotion
activates: a same-action nonlinear relational observable theorem if one completion orbit is selected
an exact theory-data ambiguity theorem if detector predictions vary across admissible quartic completions
Paper 09 lifecycle review and the nonlinear observer column of the residual atlas
body.resource_hint: OBSERVER RESERVE AFTER THE ACTIVE ORDER-FOUR CLASSIFICATION. Work in the exact action quotient first: classify completion orbits and invariants before generating another large coefficient family. Conflux may propose orbit invariants, but every promoted equivalence and response statement must be replayed in the original action-derived verifier.
notes: The order-three gate proved that identical q1 and q2 data can arise from at least two quartic completions with different q3. This item asks whether that ambiguity survives admissible action equivalences and reaches relational observables.
The item is deliberately input-pinned rather than dependency-gated so an OBSTRUCTED terminal predecessor cannot strand the resident stream.
If no complete quartic family is available, the valid terminal output is the smallest exact representation or quotient obstruction—not a sampled completion search.
